status.en: 131 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 26% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 131 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 26 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to assault civilian targets in Plateau, killing three people at a mining site and injuring others, while also kidnapping five persons and shooting two in a separate community attack. Troops intercepted an assault by Berom militiamen on a Fulani settlement in Plateau, rescuing a gunshot victim, and Nigerian forces killed two ISWAP terrorists in Adamawa, recovering weapons. A video shows Ndume being assaulted by youths in Borno, and a bandit leader, Kachalla Bello, was reported killed in Katsina. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn fortsetter å angripe sivile mål i Plateau, dreper tre personer på en gruve og skader andre, samtidig som de kidnapper fem personer og skyter to i et separat samfunnsangrep. Tropper avverget et angrep fra Berom-milits på en Fulani-bosetning i Plateau, reddet en skuddsårende, og nigerianske styrker drepte to ISWAP-terrorister i Adamawa, og gjenvant våpen. En video viser Ndume som blir angrepet av ungdom i Borno, og en banditleder, Kachalla Bello, ble rapportert drept i Katsina. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
